requirements.text: When the K semantics toolchain is selected, the semantics harness SHALL record its exact K revision, backend, executable hashes and Pel profile digest before compiling.
When Pel source is parsed by the K definition, the definition SHALL produce the selected M1 syntax and source locations independently of the TypeScript parser.
When numeric expressions execute, the K definition SHALL reproduce the finite binary64 and safe-integer restrictions of the selected Pel profile.
When a Pel value or callable list is evaluated, the K definition SHALL preserve M1 tags, pair presence, nil, quoting and one-based selection.
When a closure is called, the K definition SHALL use its captured lexical environment and the selected argument-binding rules.
When native control flow selects work, the K definition SHALL implement M1 non-strict branches, scoped loops, blocks and single-evaluation pipe injection.
When top-level dependencies become ready, the K definition SHALL reproduce ordered and automatic M1 evaluation with ready/already-emitted batches and the last-source result.
When a Pel semantic limit is reached, the K definition SHALL stop at the same pre-operation boundary and preserve the same counters as M1.
If execution encounters an invalid state or operation, then the K definition SHALL return a located domain diagnostic without inventing a host result.
When a host expression suspends, the K definition SHALL emit a bounded abstract request and accept only its matching supplied receipt.
If a receipt conflicts with source, registry, schema or request identity, then the K definition SHALL reject it without completing another request.
The K host model SHALL treat provider behavior, resource grants and publication authority as explicit external assumptions rather than derived language facts.
When a suspended configuration is serialized and restored, the K definition SHALL preserve lexical values, pending identities, selected options and consumed counters.
When completed-prefix replay or a source revision is modeled, the K definition SHALL preserve completed receipt bindings and the selected M1 replay boundary.
When an M1 child continuation is allocated or merged, the K definition SHALL preserve one-based child identity and charge child counters exactly once.
When differential conformance runs, the TypeScript harness SHALL compare independently specified expected observations, K execution and the existing M1 engine for every mapped fixture.
When conformance evidence is recorded, the TypeScript harness SHALL bind source, K definition, toolchain, runtime, corpus and comparator digests to executed case counts.
When a semantic mutation changes a required rule, the conformance suite SHALL detect the changed observable behavior.
When a mechanized claim is assessed, its claim record SHALL name its domain, assumptions, exact semantics digest, backend and checked result separately from differential evidence.
The semantics guide SHALL distinguish planned work, executable definitions, conformance evidence, mechanized claims and open correspondence assumptions.

tests.fixture: Pinned K7.1.337 and a mismatched executable hash.
tests.action: Compile a closed arithmetic definition, then repeat with the mismatched lock.
tests.expected: The matching toolchain executes the example; the mismatch is unavailable, never a passing skipped run.

tests.fixture: Every lexical and grammar row in paper-v2.json, including escapes, quoted pairs, caret, malformed numbers and Unicode spans.
tests.action: Parse with K and TypeScript independently and compare normalized trees or diagnostic locations.
tests.expected: All selected syntax cases agree; unsupported syntax is a located rejection, not an assumed AST translation.

tests.fixture: Negative zero,0.1+0.2,maximum safe integer,overflow,division by zero and out-of-range literals.
tests.action: Execute each expression and compare canonical tagged values or diagnostic codes.
tests.expected: Finite values agree bitwise after the profile normalization; invalid numbers reject. Unbounded K integers do not replace Pel numeric behavior.

tests.fixture: Nil/empty list,standalone keyword,pair with explicit nil,quoted symbol,multiple indices,slices,index zero and missing key.
tests.action: Execute positive and distinguishing negative value fixtures.
tests.expected: Exact tagged values and selection errors match M1; syntax and closures cannot become ordinary host data.

tests.fixture: Shadowed capture,partial application,required versus nil-default parameter,strict/syntax arguments,mixed named/positional call and bounded recursion.
tests.action: Execute closure fixtures with distinct capture environments and deferred calls.
tests.expected: Default timing,capture identity,partial values and call errors match M1 without dynamic scoping.

tests.fixture: If/case unselected host branch,for local scope,do/do-async,leading call chains,nested and repeated caret.
tests.action: Execute with a finite abstract host script and count emitted requests.
tests.expected: Only selected branches execute; pipe operands are evaluated once and source-defined scope is retained.

tests.fixture: Independent requests with both receipt orders,dependent definitions,conflicting symbol bindings and a slow first expression.
tests.action: Run both M1 options and all bounded receipt schedules.
tests.expected: Request identity and ready batches agree; completion order does not change the selected last-source result. Permitted independent interleavings are compared explicitly.

tests.fixture: Source,token,AST,syntax depth,reduction,iteration,call depth and value-byte limits at N-1,N,N+1.
tests.action: Run limit boundary fixtures and repeat after serialization.
tests.expected: Counters and rejection boundaries agree; administrative K rewrites do not debit Pel counters.

tests.fixture: Unknown symbol,arity/type errors,malformed closure graph,host failure and a deliberately stuck semantics rule.
tests.action: Execute invalid fixtures and remove one required rule in a temporary mutation definition.
tests.expected: Defined failures agree with M1; stuck/timeout/tool failure is harness failure, distinct from a Pel diagnostic.

tests.fixture: Two requests with separate IDs,success and failure receipts,print and natural-language predicate descriptors.
tests.action: Supply a finite data-only host script and project ordered boundary observations.
tests.expected: No provider or shell runs; requests,receipt consumption,pending sets and output observations match M1.

tests.fixture: Wrong request/profile/registry,duplicate conflicting receipt,closure-bearing provider value and missing receipt.
tests.action: Inject each invalid receipt at the same suspension boundary.
tests.expected: Exact mismatches fail; missing external evidence stays suspended. No fabricated cancellation or authority is accepted.

tests.fixture: Abstract retry/race/checkpoint handlers and a publication-shaped ordinary data value.
tests.action: Execute request scripts with success,unknown and rejected host responses.
tests.expected: Only the supplied abstract response is modeled; no budget authority,remote completion or publication milestone is inferred from source data.

tests.fixture: Nested closures,syntax arguments,ready/already-emitted effects and malformed environment references.
tests.action: Roundtrip K state and the M1 continuation through the declared correspondence projection.
tests.expected: Equivalent configurations resume to identical observations; broken graph/profile bindings reject. Raw wire-byte equality is required only where explicitly specified.

tests.fixture: Completed pure prefix,pending suffix,changed executed effect argument,unchanged closure capture and changed options.
tests.action: Replay the retained prefix and compare accepted/rejected revisions with M1.
tests.expected: No completed host request is emitted twice; invalid revisions reject and original counters remain charged.

tests.fixture: Two child closures,duplicate merge,cancelled/failed child and nested child replay.
tests.action: Compare start-child and merge-child observations with the M1 public APIs.
tests.expected: Child identities,remaining limits and parent charges agree; M4 retry/race policy remains outside this language-model proof domain.

tests.fixture: All paper-v2 rows and current M1 control,closure,limits,host,replay and child regression cases.
tests.action: Execute the closed corpus plus fixed-seed bounded programs using the same explicit host schedules.
tests.expected: Every included constructor has positive and negative cases; missing rows or mismatches fail and retain a minimal source/receipt counterexample.

tests.fixture: One real execution report,missing K executable,stale source hash and interrupted child process.
tests.action: Run and validate reports with finite timeout/output bounds and scoped cleanup.
tests.expected: Only actually executed cases count; missing prerequisites are unavailable, interrupted cases incomplete, and stale evidence cannot pass.

tests.fixture: Mutations make indexing zero-based,evaluate both if branches,recapture closures dynamically,duplicate pipe effects or reset replay counters.
tests.action: Run each temporary mutation against its distinguishing unchanged fixture.
tests.expected: Every mutation is detected; merely parsing or compiling a definition cannot pass conformance.

tests.fixture: Claims for at-most-once receipt consumption and nondecreasing counters in a finite closed host-script domain,plus a deliberately false invariant.
tests.action: Use the pinned proof backend for the selected claims; retain counterexample,timeout or unsupported results.
tests.expected: Only discharged scoped claims say proved; the false control is not proved. No full TypeScript/K equivalence,host safety or termination theorem is inferred.

tests.fixture: No implementation,trace-only results,scoped proof results and a changed semantics digest.
tests.action: Render the status table and verify linked claim/trace artifacts and changed-domain invalidation.
tests.expected: PLANNED remains the current sprint state until implementation evidence exists. Changed semantics reopen affected claims; historical evidence remains intact.
